post.text:
Fun fact.

Every mobile phone has an average of 36 mg of gold and to extract this small portion, through traditional mining, 3 kg of earth have to be removed.

This is the process used for extracting it.

- Science Guy (@pradyumn93): Recycling old phones for gold is far more efficient than mining ore. One metric ton of discarded smartphones contains up to eighty times more gold than a metric ton of gold ore taken from the earth. This means urban e-waste has become one of the richest gold deposits on the planet. Modern recovery labs call this “urban mining,” and in some countries it now produces more precious metals than traditional mines, all while reducing environmental damage and chemical waste. (16 likes)
- Dcntrlyzr (@dcntrlyzr): Oh!! When you say it like that: the harm to the environment for each mobile is quite a lot Also, is it worth the effort and money that goes into extraction?? Like a get-rich-quick scheme OR a viable long term business?? 🤔🤔 (14 likes)
- Doolly Noted ✏️ (@doollynoted): Note: Every phone has ~36 mg of gold, worth about $3–$4 at today’s prices. To extract it profitably, you need to process thousands of phones in a proper e-waste facility with acid leaching or cyanide. Doing it from one or a few phones at home costs way more than the gold is worth and is dangerous. So basically, it’s never worth it for individuals. (12 likes)
